topics.topic: Representation of an absent runner report in ExecutionObservation
questions: Must ExecutionObservation.report become RunnerReport | None so judge_execution can represent and detect that no returned message was read, or must the no-returned-message case be represented by a concrete RunnerReport value and specified accordingly?

How can execute_function construct the required ExecutionObservation and call judge_execution when no runner report was read; must report become RunnerReport | None, or must execute_function synthesize a specified RunnerReport?

How can judge_execution detect that no report message was read when observation.report is required and cannot be None; must the field be optional, or must the no-message condition be represented by a specified RunnerReport value?

How can judge_execution observe that no returned message was read when ExecutionObservation requires a non-optional RunnerReport and has no field representing an absent message; must report become optional or must the no-message condition be represented by another declared field?

quotes: ExecutionObservation fields (exact, no others exist): timed_out: bool, exited_abnormally: bool, cleanup_confirmed: bool, wall_time_ms: int, memory_bytes: int, report: RunnerReport

It MUST return judge_execution of an ExecutionObservation of what it saw — whether the deadline passed, whether the runner exited abnormally (killed by a signal, SIGXFSZ included, or a non-zero status), whether cleanup was confirmed, the elapsed wall_time_ms, the peak memory_bytes and the decoded report — with the output ports and the bounds.
crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read;
judgement.why: The required non-optional report and required decoded report cannot represent the explicitly recognized case in which no report message was read.

topics.topic: Handling missing json_text when counting JSON ReturnedOutput bytes
questions: For a ReturnedOutput whose form is json but whose permitted json_text value is None, canonical_bytes cannot be called with the declared str argument; must the model require json_text for json form, or must the counting rule exclude malformed value outputs before calling canonical_bytes?

quotes: def canonical_bytes(json_text: str) -> bytes
ReturnedOutput fields (exact, no others exist): port: str, form: ReturnedForm, json_text: str | None, contents: tuple[bytes, ...]

The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.

contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded.
judgement.divergence: One implementer treats a json-form output with json_text None as a contract violation without counting JSON bytes; another passes None to canonical_bytes or treats that failure as a crash. The caller notices a different SandboxResult outcome and potentially different resources_used.output_bytes.
judgement.why: The texts permit json_text to be None but do not specify how counting precedes or handles validation of that malformed JSON output.

topics.topic: How assemble_mapped_lists obtains each MappedList port's stored schema and cardinality
questions: The required schema depends on the port's value_schema and cardinality, but MappedList contains only the port name and element references; must MappedList provide the Port metadata, or must the requirement define how the stored schema is derived from the referenced elements?
Must MappedList provide the Port or its stored schema and cardinality, or must assemble_mapped_lists derive the item schema solely from the element StoredValues?

quotes: assemble_mapped_lists: [BEHAVIOR] MUST build, for each MappedList in the order given, the list its elements' outputs make in element order, and write and publish nothing: a value list is one StoredValue whose bytes are canonical_bytes of the list of the elements' values — each read with read_value_bytes —, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) as items, of the class highest_disclosure_class gives for the elements' StoredValues — read through read_records with one RecordsById naming their value_ids —, its value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent; a file list is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements' SpooledFilesRefs.
MappedList fields (exact, no others exist): port: str, elements: tuple[PortRef, ...]
StoredValue fields (exact, no others exist): value_id: str, value_digest: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, value_schema: str, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass, size_bytes: int
judgement.divergence: One implementer derives the item schema from an element StoredValue's value_schema, while another treats that schema as already array-wrapped for a many port or cannot assemble without separate Port metadata; downstream fit checks and callers notice different value_schema and value_id values, especially through an extra array-schema layer.
judgement.why: The required schema depends on Port metadata that MappedList does not contain, and the text does not specify a unique derivation from the element references.

topics.topic: How refused_by_owner affects run status and next-node selection
questions: If a refused_by_owner record coexists with a derived draft or otherwise-ready node, must the status be refused with no next node or running?
When a refused_by_owner record exists and nothing waits, must the status be refused or failed?

quotes: a run with any refused_by_owner NodeExecution has status refused and no next node.
While a draft is derived or a node is ready the status is running.
judgement.why: The unconditional refused rule conflicts with the unconditional running rule when a refused record coexists with a draft or ready node.

topics.topic: How an operation element's conclusion is determined
questions: Must an operation element be judged only by operation_element_conclusion, or may its skipped_by_guard/upstream_failed NodeExecution status conclude it?

quotes: an operation element's is operation_element_conclusion of its element under the context — ElementFailed is failed whatever its status, ElementWaiting waits and its dependants wait, ElementNotReached is not concluded; an operation element is judged by that answer alone, not by its NodeExecution status, which stays outcome_unknown after the owner's resolution;
a skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed record concludes its node so;
judgement.why: One passage makes the imported operation conclusion exclusive, while the other permits two NodeExecution statuses to conclude the operation node.

topics.topic: What source representation RunPlan.outputs uses for a flow output sourced directly from a flow input
questions: Must the flow output be an InputSource such as a RecordedSource wrapping the StoredValuesRef, or may a StoredValuesRef itself be placed in RunPlan.outputs?

quotes: RunPlan fields (exact, no others exist): conclusions: tuple[ElementState, ...], edges: tuple[EdgeState, ...], derived: tuple[NodeExecutionDraft, ...], next_node: ReadyNode | None, waiting: tuple[WaitingPoint, ...], outputs: tuple[InputSource, ...], missing_outputs: tuple[MissingOutput, ...], status: RunStatus

Each element's sources are one per input port in port name order: a RecordedSource for a flow input's StoredValuesRef, a constant's StoredValuesRef or the output ref of an unmapped succeeded node on the enabled edge — from its NodeExecution or its ElementSucceeded outputs —;
A flow output's source is formed the same way; an output reached by an edge straight from a flow input is that input's StoredValuesRef (A13 rule 3).
judgement.why: The output field requires InputSource values and the same-way rule implies RecordedSource, but the direct-flow-input rule says the output is the StoredValuesRef itself.

topics.topic: When an unguarded edge sourced from a flow input becomes enabled
questions: Must an unguarded edge from a flow input be enabled immediately, or remain unenablable because its empty-string source is not a node that can conclude succeeded?

quotes: An edge with no guard is enabled once its source concluded succeeded;

The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them — a flow input or output endpoint is the node_id empty string (A05 rule 2) —, constants to their port — a FlowConstant's value is the value_id composition wrote —, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every enabled edge.
judgement.why: The first passage conditions every unguarded edge on a succeeded source, while the second requires flow inputs to be delivered despite their empty-string source not being a node that can conclude.

topics.topic: Whether an empty mapped list contains a synthetic element
questions: Must an empty mapped list have no elements because elements are list positions, or must it have the specified synthetic element without map_index?

quotes: a mapped node over an empty list is ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index whose sources are the node's inputs;
judgement.why: The explicit empty-list special case requires one synthetic element without a map index.

topics.topic: Whether and how a synthetic mapped element receives its required map_over source without a map_index

quotes: a mapped node over an empty list is ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index whose sources are the node's inputs;
a ListElementSource with the list's own source and the element's map_index for a mapped element's map_over port.
ListElementSource fields (exact, no others exist): source_kind: Literal['list_element'], port: str, list: ListSource, map_index: int
